resources.string: Counts how many Instagram Reels you scroll. It only works inside the Instagram app and only notices when you swipe to a new Reel. It never reads captions, messages, usernames or what you watch, and does not record your screen.

Doomboard uses Android's Accessibility Service to count your Instagram Reels.

What it uses: only inside the Instagram app, it notices when you swipe to a new Reel, from the screen's layout (which part is scrolling).

What it never does: it does not read captions, messages, usernames or what you watch, does not record your screen, and does nothing in any other app.

Your counts stay on this phone unless you join the leaderboard.

On the next screen, tap Doomboard and turn it on.

Doomboard counts your Reels on this phone. If you join the global leaderboard, it shares only your nickname and daily totals (reels and minutes), never what you watch. Leave any time and your data is deleted.
